To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ITIES can be decorated in a controlled way with a variety of molecules, nano objects and nanomaterials.
the electrochemical control of the interface is the key to the development of functionalized soft interfaces.
(i) electrochemical methods allow to control the assembly of molecules and nanoparticles at soft interfaces and (ii) the electrochemical methods allow the in situ generation of nano objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of electrochemical methods for the synthesis and characterization of molecular and nano-structured materials.
the electrochemistry of soft interfaces and more specifically with the development of new strategies for the electrochemical modification of such soft electrified interfaces.
the design, synthesis, characterization and application of molecular materials and nanoscale devices for the control of electron and ion transfer reactions at the molecular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the soft interface can be considered as an ideal playground for the study of the charge transfer processes and that the electrochemical control of the interface properties is an extremely powerful tool for the investigation of the charge transfer mechanisms.
soft interfaces are the most versatile platforms for electrochemistry, with the potential for a large number of applications in the fields of electrocatalysis and biosensing.
electrochemists can decorate soft electrified interfaces at the molecular and nanoscopic scales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soft interfaces are not only interesting for the fundamental investigation of electrochemical phenomena, but they can also be used for a large variety of applications.
the ITIES can be decorated by a wide range of materials and that these materials can be used as electrochemical sensors.
electrochemical control of the soft interface is a very promising tool in order to design functional interfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soft electrified interface is a unique tool to control the organization of matter and to develop new materials.
the electrochemically induced modification of soft interfaces constitutes an efficient tool for the development of novel functional materials and devices for electrochemistry.
soft electrified interfaces are versatile tools to be used in the development of new electrochemical sensors and in the study of charge transfer reactions.
